official_sources.finding: PROJ supports time-dependent coordinate operations including kinematic Helmert transformations with parameter rates.
A time-dependent Helmert operation uses a central transformation epoch t_epoch.
Time-dependent transformations are commonly used between static plate-fixed and dynamic reference frames.
The observation epoch can be carried as the fourth coordinate component during a transformation.
Since PROJ 9.4 a dynamic CRS can be qualified with a coordinate epoch using CRS@epoch syntax.
The PROJ documentation describes CoordinateMetadata as the generic mechanism for attaching epoch metadata to a dynamic CRS in newer APIs.
Coordinate-operation APIs can report whether per-coordinate input time is required.
Older PROJ behavior could treat an epoch supplied on the reverse transformation as input time, so runtime version and epoch semantics must be recorded.
projinfo --s_epoch specifies the source coordinate epoch as a decimal year for a dynamic CRS.
projinfo --t_epoch specifies the target coordinate epoch as a decimal year for a dynamic CRS.
cs2cs supports explicit source-coordinate epoch with --s_epoch for dynamic CRS input.
cs2cs supports explicit target-coordinate epoch with --t_epoch for dynamic CRS output.
The deformation operation central epoch is expressed in decimal years.
For deformation operations t_epoch and fixed dt are mutually exclusive policies.
When t_epoch is used, observation time from the input coordinate determines the applied deformation interval.
proj_coordoperation_requires_per_coordinate_input_time reports whether a coordinate operation needs valid input time.
For time-dependent Helmert, proj_trans may still execute with missing time by falling back to the transformation central epoch.
PROJ pipelines support 4D spatiotemporal coordinates with three spatial components and one temporal component.
A PROJ pipeline can explicitly convert temporal units such as GPS week to decimal year before a Helmert step.
Temporal units can be converted back after a time-dependent step, so input and operation time units are separate provenance.
Kinematic Helmert transformations require an observation time and a central epoch.
Helmert temporal input is expressed in decimal years.
Time-dependent Helmert parameters are propagated as base parameter plus rate times observation-minus-central-epoch interval.
Specifying a rate parameter activates the kinematic form of the Helmert transformation.
cct is a 4D coordinate conversion and transformation utility.
cct -t can supply a fixed observation time for all input coordinates.
cct -z can supply a fixed observation height independently of observation time.
cct maps input columns to x,y,z,t explicitly, making column order part of replay provenance.
cct can instantiate an explicit coordinate operation definition rather than relying on implicit CRS-to-CRS selection.
For time-dependent operations the fourth coordinate component v[3] is the decimal-year coordinate epoch of input.
HUGE_VAL represents absence of a time ordinate in the documented C++ transformation example.
PROJ operation APIs likewise define v[3] as decimal-year input coordinate epoch for time-dependent operations.
CRS-to-CRS transformation computes candidate coordinate operations before execution, so operation choice must be provenance-bound.
Candidate-operation computation is metadata-driven and can yield one or several operation pipelines.
OS ETRS89 geodetic input formats can include an optional ETRS89 ellipsoidal height.
OS National Grid coordinate format uses metre eastings/northings and can include optional ODN height in metres.
UK geospatial guidance states ETRS89 accounts for plate tectonic movement by adoption of an epoch or point in time.
The 1989 in ETRS89 refers to the original realization from which later realizations are based.
ETRS89 is widely used in the UK for GNSS positioning and mapping.
The UK standards register lists EPSG:4937 for ETRS89 latitude, longitude and ellipsoidal height.
The UK standards register lists EPSG:9452 for ETRS89 plus British and Irish mean-sea-level height systems including ODN.
The UK standards register identifies EPSG:7953 as the OSTN15 ETRS89-to-British-National-Grid transformation.
The UK standards register identifies EPSG:9916 as the OSGM15 ETRS89-ellipsoidal-height to mean-sea-level-height transformation.
The underlying GNSS coordinate reference frame for positioning in Great Britain is ETRS89.
OSTN15 links ETRS89 GNSS positions to OSGB36 British National Grid.
OSGM15 links ETRS89 ellipsoidal heights to mean-sea-level-based height systems such as ODN.
OS Net uses ETRS89 as its coordinate system.
OSGB36 National Grid and Ordnance Datum can be realized from ETRS89 through precise transformation and geoid modeling.
The OS transformation between ETRS89/WGS84 and OSGB36/ODN uses OSTN15/OSGM15.
OS recommends retaining archived ETRS89 geodetic coordinates so transformations can be revisited later.
OS describes ETRS89 as having less than 5 mm relative reference-frame distortion across Great Britain.
OSTN15 updated the transformation grid partly to account for a slight change in the realization of ETRS89 in Great Britain.
OS advises that coordinates produced with OSTN02/OSGM02 should be back-transformed to ETRS89 before forward transformation with OSTN15/OSGM15 when reconciling old and new models.
Archived ETRS89 coordinates avoid that legacy back-transformation step when relating old and new transformation models.
The OS national GNSS network realizes the ETRS89 reference frame for Great Britain.
OS uses OSGM15 to provide access to ODN and other height datums via ETRS89.
